# IMP-014.1 private primitive diagnostics contract

Implementation baseline: `b5ccd06b9c6a6dd8cfde6f344fc34e1a953f2d3d`.
Specification baseline: [documentation c7d56e5](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-Documentation/blob/c7d56e5bb029eb4ef10c1ceaed0e9bfdfae96584/docs/source/docs/implementation-prompts.md#imp-014-1).
Architecture remains **0.5**. Diagnostic record and catalog fingerprint schemas are
**1**. IR, admission/artifact identity, repository, jobs, citizen identity, leases,
outcomes and inference broker schemas remain unchanged.

## Compiler, catalog and research ownership

`SkillCompiler.Failure` preserves `diagnostics()` and its original constructor.
Its additive `unsupportedPrimitive()` optionally contains one
`UnsupportedPrimitiveReference`: validated requested ID/version/fingerprint,
existing `UNKNOWN_PRIMITIVE` diagnostic/path, ordinal observed argument types and
optional complete catalog fingerprint. It contains no candidate-defined names,
values, executable callback or inferred missing-signature type.

Evidence is produced only after locally validating call keys, requested reference,
bounded arguments/expressions/symbols and result binding. Compilation remains pure
and fail-fast. It proves absence of the requested pair in the lookup snapshot;
it does not prove whole-program validity, absence at every version or capability
impossibility. Known-pair fingerprint/type errors, dependency failures and malformed
references retain their existing diagnostics and carry no positive absence proof.

`PrimitiveDiagnostics.completeCatalog` creates a complete immutable
`CatalogSnapshot`, with at most 128 unique signatures. The concrete owner asserts
completeness. Lookup and fingerprint use the same snapshot. Fingerprint schema 1
hashes big-endian schema/count and sorted length-prefixed UTF-8 canonical signature
records, including parameter names/types/bounds, result type and sorted effects.
`KernelSession` supplies all eleven `GatewayPrimitives.all()` signatures. Metadata
failure falls back to the original runtime catalog and omits observation. Prompt
subsets supply no absence proof. A dynamic catalog must supply an atomic complete
snapshot through this seam before enabling collection.

`ResearchAdmissionController` preserves its original constructor with a no-op
sink and adds the trusted `PrimitiveDiagnostics.Sink` overload. Accepted generation
identity, role, owner, epoch, deadline, cancellation and current authority gates
precede observation. Current authority is rechecked after asynchronous compilation.

Typed absence terminates `NOT_ADMITTED / UNSUPPORTED_PRIMITIVE` before repair.
Other eligible failures retain bounded repair. Supplied `evaluateCandidate`
inputs receive the same rejection without contributing AI demand. The static worker
prepares exact submitted UTF-8 candidate SHA-256, safe provider metadata and the
registered request shape. The owner offers one bounded immutable observation per
authorized rejected generated attempt. Missing catalog identity invokes the fixed
local omission counter. Sink failures never change outcomes, ledgers or effects.
No diagnostic-triggered inference, retry, fixture, trial or publication exists.

## Provider compatibility

`Generation.Descriptor.protocol` accepts `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`;
existing model/digest and local endpoint restrictions remain. Diagnostics allowlist
ASCII metadata up to 128 bytes and mark unsafe model/digest values omitted.

`LocalGenerationAdapter` preserves compact body-object lowering and passes full
IR body lists through existing bounded strict envelope/dependency gates. Unknown
compact names remain malformed. Full IR is untrusted compiler input, never
execution or admission authority. The sink is independent of Ollama transport.

## Service and lifecycle

`PrimitiveDiagnosticService` implements `Sink`. One owned service and dedicated
daemon `cognitivecraft-primitive-diagnostics` serves all production session
controllers/scopes. It does not use the world-store worker, provider worker, broker
queue or repository locks. Default OFF creates no diagnostic worker or files.

`beginTick()` resets the session-wide eight-offer allowance. `offer()` reserves
atomic bounded slots and publishes to a nonblocking queue without I/O, source
parsing, HMAC, future wait or worker-held monitor. Envelopes contain trusted
correlation, safe typed proof and bounded projections; never raw source, request
values, prompt, conversation or Minecraft objects.

The worker runs at most once per 1000 ms without catch-up. Replay owns its final
cycle's inspection budget before normal maintenance begins. Aggregation uses the
canonical length-delimited tuple of schema/day/world/scope/principal/capability/
complete catalog/requested pair and fingerprint/compiler code. Path, model, source
bytes and attempt IDs are excluded. The first representative is immutable; latest
event, lastSeen, revision and observed-attempt count advance. Recent dedup uses
attempt/generation HMACs in a bounded FIFO. Independent broker subscribers count
as independent observed attempts, including when one physical inference is shared.

Sequence exhaustion stops intake. Counts saturate; revision exhaustion seals the
row. Loss counters saturate and remain independent of inference accounting.
Cached immutable status has no player, command, autocomplete, packet or HTTP route.

`KernelSession` opens collection independently of authoritative store readiness,
resets intake once per server tick and starts asynchronous closure before its
normal storage cleanup. Trusted fixture injection seams do not alter public routes.

## Privacy and storage schema

`PrimitiveDiagnosticCodec` owns bounded strict schema-1 UTF-8 JSONL encoding/
validation through Gson. A row is a cumulative snapshot with `aggregateId`,
`revision`, `occurrences`, UTC day bucket and immutable first `representative`.
The representative includes candidate SHA-256, accepted provider/role, compiler
path/code, ordinal types and optional redacted projections. Attempt/generation and
world/scope/principal identifiers use domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 with a verified
private 32-byte salt. Requested fingerprint is unverified requested metadata.
`latestEventId` is a server session UUID plus positive checked sequence.

Projections contain registered capability/parameter types and reconstructed
rejected-reference/type structure only. All candidate-defined names become
ordinals; all values/context are fixed redaction markers. No raw candidate is
reparsed by diagnostics. Excerpts require trusted explicit scope opt-in. Limits
apply after JSON escaping/UTF-8 encoding, with typed byte/omission/truncation flags.
Optional projections are dropped first, then an oversized minimum envelope drops.
Malformed UTF-8, duplicate fields, unknown fields, invalid Unicode, noninteger
numbers, excessive depth/nodes and forged required metadata are rejected.

`PrimitiveDiagnosticStore` implements the worker-only
`PrimitiveDiagnosticStorePort`. Root:
`<world>/data/cognitivecraft/diagnostics/primitive/v1/`.
All diagnostic directories are POSIX 0700, files 0600, with exact account ownership,
or verified owner-only ACLs on another supported filesystem. Shared world/data
ancestors may be created concurrently by existing stores; they are verified as
owned directories without imposing diagnostic permissions on them. Symlink
ancestors/entries, unsafe privacy, excessive/unknown files and exclusive writer
lock contention disable persistence. Paths are fixed server-generated names.

`salt.bin` is exactly 32 private bytes and reused across restarts. A missing or
corrupt salt with any history disables collection; it is never silently replaced.
An explicit host reset must remove diagnostic-only history before creating a
fresh empty store. No diagnostic reset touches admitted artifacts or journals.

At most eight fixed `segment-0.jsonl` through `segment-7.jsonl` files are retained.
Each holds one UTC-day bucket. Rotate before exceeding size; prune only known
closed diagnostic segments. A snapshot uses one append call; a partial write
stops persistence without retry. Replay selects the highest valid revision per
aggregate, never sums cumulative snapshots or replays research. Truncated/
malformed records are counted and ignored within caps. Future schemas disable
the session, remain inactive and consume quota; no quarantine copies are created.

Effective time is max(observed UTC, startup effective UTC + monotonic elapsed).
Startup accepts retained timestamps at most 300000 ms ahead of UTC; larger future
timestamps disable collection. Backward clock changes never prolong live expiry.
Maintenance expires in-memory rows, active/closed segments and reports even when
idle. Expired rows are suppressed before attempted physical deletion.

Disk, permission, lock, serialization and append failures stop persistence for
the session. Bounded memory aggregation may continue; retention deletion failure
disables collection. There is no reopen/retry loop or replacement worker. The only
warning is fixed text, at most once per 60 seconds, without payload/exception details.

## Finite ceilings and zero policy

| Resource | Schema-1 hard maximum |
|---|---:|
| Encoded record including newline | 8192 bytes |
| Escaped request / candidate projections | 1024 / 4096 bytes |
| Pending queue / reserved payload | 128 / 1048576 bytes |
| Offers per global server tick | 8 |
| Per-second dequeue / inspection / writes | 32 / 32 / 16 |
| Per-cycle written bytes | 131072 |
| Aggregates / recent dedup entries | 512 / 1024 |
| Segment bytes / count | 1048576 / 8 |
| Entire directory including unknown/temp/report files | 10485760 bytes / 16 files |
| Replay segment bytes / records | 8388608 / 65536 |
| Advisory report rows / bytes | 100 / 65536 |
| Async shutdown events / bytes / deadline | 32 / 131072 / 2000 ms |
| Logical retention | 604800000 ms from fixed day start |

`Policy` accepts only lower allowances. Negative, above-ceiling, overflow and
inconsistent size relationships reject configuration without preventing gameplay.
Zero core collection capacity disables collection; zero excerpt/report capacity
omits/disables that optional facility; zero drain capacity drops pending work.
The documented working reservation is
`2 MiB + queue*8192 + aggregates*24576 + dedup*512`:
**16252928 bytes (15.5 MiB)** at defaults, excluding fixed JVM/class overhead.
It covers envelopes, rows/views/encoding scratch and recent dedup. This is a
bounded reservation argument, not a claim to measure total JVM RSS.

`closeAsync()` immediately stops intake and returns the same future on repeated
calls. Drain/drop is asynchronous and finite; the server never joins the worker.
A hung filesystem call may outlive the deadline until released/process exit,
and an already started write may finish later. No replacement thread is spawned.
Offline time, blocked I/O and failed deletion cannot guarantee physical wall-clock
erasure; logical reads suppress expired data.

## Trusted startup configuration and offline inspection

`PrimitiveDiagnosticConfig.read` accepts startup environment only:

- `COGNITIVECRAFT_PRIMITIVE_DIAGNOSTICS=off|metadata|excerpts` (default off).
- `COGNITIVECRAFT_PRIMITIVE_DIAGNOSTIC_SCOPES=<world UUID>/<domain UUID>,...`
  for excerpts; explicit trusted list up to 64, no wildcard or duplicates.
- `COGNITIVECRAFT_PRIMITIVE_DIAGNOSTIC_<Limit enum name>=<lower integer>`
  for optional lower allowances.

Invalid configuration installs OFF with one fixed startup warning.

After shutting down the writer, an authorized host invokes:

```bash
java -cp "<production-jar>:<gson-2.10.1-jar>" \
  dev.aivillages.core.kernel.PrimitiveDiagnosticReport "<world-root>"
```

Windows uses `;` as the classpath separator. Optional trailing `rows bytes`
arguments lower report limits. The CLI validates private files and exclusively
locks the existing store; it never creates a replacement salt or invokes a
provider, gateway or gameplay repository. It writes only `report.json` through
one reserved private `report.json.tmp` and atomic move.

Reports group by requested ID/version and observed catalog, use a bounded trusted
capability-family map with Unmapped fallback, and rank by attempts/capabilities/
recency/ID/version/catalog. Exports omit private correlation, candidate hashes,
models and excerpts. They explicitly mark incomplete counts and unknown crash
losses. Reports inherit the earliest included bucket's expiry; they are advisory
human review inputs with no executable/planner/admission or new capability authority.

[Acceptance evidence and exact test mapping](IMP-014.1-report.md).
